topics.title: Closures, Lexical Scope & this
topics.summary: Understand how functions remember surrounding bindings, how this is determined by call style, and when arrow functions intentionally capture lexical this.

concepts.name: Closures
concepts.explanation: A function keeps access to the lexical environment where it was created even after that outer function has returned. This enables private state and function factories.

concepts.name: this
concepts.explanation: For normal functions, this depends on how the function is called. Method calls, constructors, explicit bind/call/apply, and plain calls can produce different values.

concepts.name: Arrow functions
concepts.explanation: Arrow functions do not create their own this, arguments, or prototype. They are excellent callbacks but are not drop-in replacements for every method/constructor.

topics.challenge: Create a function factory whose returned function or object method remembers private state from the outer function.
topics.hint: Declare the state in the outer function and return a function that reads or changes it.

topics.title: Prototypes, Classes & Object Design
topics.summary: Connect class syntax to JavaScript's prototype model and design objects with constructors, methods, inheritance, private fields, and composition.

concepts.name: Prototype chain
concepts.explanation: Property lookup walks an object's own properties and then its prototype chain. Methods shared through a prototype avoid copying the same function onto every instance.

concepts.name: Class syntax
concepts.explanation: class offers constructor, instance methods, static members, fields, private #fields, inheritance with extends, and super calls.

concepts.name: Composition
concepts.explanation: Inheritance is one tool, not the default answer. Small objects/functions composed around capabilities often reduce fragile superclass relationships.

topics.challenge: Create a class with a constructor, one private field, one method, and one getter.
topics.hint: Private fields begin with # and can only be accessed inside the class body.

topics.title: Promises, async/await & Fetch
topics.summary: Represent future results with promises, compose asynchronous work, handle errors, and avoid blocking or deeply nested callbacks.

concepts.name: Promises
concepts.explanation: A promise is pending, fulfilled, or rejected. then/catch/finally compose outcomes without exposing manual completion to consumers.

concepts.name: async/await
concepts.explanation: async functions return promises. await pauses that async function until a promise settles while allowing the JavaScript runtime to continue other work.

concepts.name: Fetch
concepts.explanation: fetch returns a promise for an HTTP Response. HTTP error status codes do not reject automatically, so check response.ok before parsing data.

topics.challenge: Write an async function that awaits fetch, checks response.ok, and returns parsed JSON.
topics.hint: Network failure can reject fetch, but an HTTP 404/500 still requires an explicit response.ok check.

topics.title: Map, Set, Weak Collections & Data Modeling
topics.summary: Choose collection types based on identity, uniqueness, key flexibility, and lifetime semantics instead of forcing everything into arrays or plain objects.

concepts.name: Map
concepts.explanation: Map accepts keys of any value type, preserves insertion order, exposes size, and has explicit get/set/has/delete methods.

concepts.name: Set
concepts.explanation: Set stores unique values. It is useful for membership tests and deduplicating values without manually scanning an array.

concepts.name: WeakMap/WeakSet
concepts.explanation: Weak collections hold object keys weakly and are not enumerable. They are useful for associating metadata with objects without extending object lifetime.

topics.challenge: Create a Set for unique completed items and a Map that stores at least two key/value scores.
topics.hint: Use Set.add/has and Map.set/get rather than array methods.

topics.title: Modules, Regular Expressions & Internationalization
topics.summary: Work with richer standard-library capabilities while keeping parsing, formatting, and module boundaries explicit.

concepts.name: Regular expressions
concepts.explanation: RegExp can search and validate text patterns, but complex patterns should be documented and tested. Do not use regex where a proper parser is required.

concepts.name: Intl
concepts.explanation: Intl.NumberFormat, DateTimeFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, Collator, and related APIs format/compare values according to locale rules.

concepts.name: Module loading
concepts.explanation: Static import is analyzable up front. dynamic import() returns a promise and can load optional code only when needed.

topics.challenge: Create one regular expression test and format a number with Intl.NumberFormat.
topics.hint: Keep validation patterns small enough to explain; use Intl instead of manually concatenating currency symbols and separators.
